techniques.name: One sheet, one camera
techniques.description: All panels laid out on one big stage in a 4 by 2 grid. A single camera transform moves between regions with a heavy ease; motion blur only during moves. Allows the reveal at the end at no extra cost.
techniques.routeReason: RegionCamera and regionTransform map regions to a stage already; Shutter gives blur only in the move windows. whipPan does not fit, because it is a transition between two separate scenes and could not reveal a shared sheet. Rendering all eight panels each frame could be slow; cull those off screen.

ease.name: cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)
evidence: visuals/a1/t-slide1.jpg F169-F181 diff 11.8, 19.6, 22.8, 25.1, 24.5, 24.7, 22.6, 16.4, 13.6, 11.4, 10.6, 8.3, 5.7: peak speed by the 4th frame, then a decay twice as long

sound.note: Each slide starts after the last word of a sentence has begun and the next chapter's first word falls in the slide's last frames. Whether music sits under the voice was not established.

techniques.name: Land on the empty panel
techniques.description: Next panel is empty when the move ends. First object appears 5 to 20 frames later, once the new sentence has started.
techniques.routeReason: Only timing: cue objects from word times.

evidence: visuals/a1/t-slide1.jpg F181-F186: panel settles empty at F181, first object enters at F186 (6.20 s)

sound.note: The first object follows the first word of the new sentence (5.97 s word, 6.20 s object).

techniques.name: Die-cut figures with a white edge and shadow
techniques.description: Black-and-white engraving-style subjects with a white die-cut rim and small shadow, placed at slight angles. Puppet motion on a single limb.
techniques.routeReason: The art is the expensive part, and it must look like one hand. It likely needs generated images with a fixed style, at a cost, or public-domain engravings via resource-discovery. Rim and shadow are simple in Remotion using SVG filters. Consistency of generated images across the set is untested here. The block paper-collage-assemble already gives cut-outs a keyline and a paper shadow on twos; the rim width and the one-limb puppet are still missing.

techniques.name: Stamp slam
techniques.description: Big and translucent to small and solid in 4 frames (F1015-F1019 for the first), rotated, with no bounce visible. Ink colour multiplies on the paper. On the first, the whole frame shifts for about 4 frames after contact (F1019-F1022, diff 15-19 across every edge), read as an impact jolt; that reading is inferred. The second and third were not stripped frame by frame.
techniques.routeReason: A track on scale and opacity; mix-blend-mode multiply.

evidence: visuals/a1/t-stamp1.jpg F1015-F1019: faint and large at F1015, solid and small by F1019

ease.name: power2.in
evidence: visuals/a1/t-stamp1.jpg F1015-F1019 diff 3.0, 0.6, 1.5, 1.4: too few frames to fit

techniques.name: A physical stamp hits and leaves
techniques.description: A wooden stamp is already low at F957, leaving the mark, then rises out of frame by F969. The mark stays.
techniques.routeReason: A cut-out moved by a track.

techniques.name: Pasted scrap lettering
techniques.description: Each letter on its own scrap with its own face and colour, landing with slight rotation 2-3 frames apart.
techniques.routeReason: Glyphs handle splitting and stagger. Faces must have Cyrillic if used in Russian, so fonts need checking.

evidence: visuals/a1/t-letters.jpg F61-F79: diff 8-10 per frame while scraps land, decaying to under 1 by F82

typography.entry: one letter per pasted scrap, 2-3 frames apart, slight rotation
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 3.02-3.52 box x 0.408 w 0.556 h 0.150

techniques.name: Quill writing and hand circle
techniques.description: A pen follows the writing as script appears along its path; a circle is then drawn in red.
techniques.routeReason: Needs stroked paths of the script, as a font alone will not reveal in stroke order. This takes prepared SVG per line.

typography.entry: written in stroke order behind a pen, in step with the voice
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 4.02-4.52 box x 0.487 w 0.384 h 0.158

sound.note: Writing runs 2.8-3.7 s against words at 2.87-3.53 s.

techniques.name: Parts converge, white flash, the product appears
techniques.description: Three part-objects with plus signs between them slide together onto the third (F705-F715), the product page replaces them at F716, the whole frame bleaches nearly to white for one frame (F717, diff 37.6) and returns over two (F718-F719), then the page flickers into place by F729. Portrait and heading never move.
techniques.routeReason: Three translations and a one-frame white overlay with a short decay; the swap happens under the flash so no morph is needed.

techniques.name: Pins spreading from one point
techniques.description: One pin at F810 (27.0 s), a 0.6 s pause, then more pins from F829 (27.63 s) every 2-3 frames outward to at least F856 (28.53 s), each a single-frame pop with no scale animation. Diffs about 4 on pop frames against 0.5 elsewhere.
techniques.routeReason: Dots on a map from data, ordered by distance.

evidence: visuals/a1/t-pins.jpg F810 first pin; F829-F856 pops every 2-3 frames (diff about 4 on pop frames, 0.5 between)

ease.name: steps(14)
evidence: visuals/a1/t-pins.jpg F829, F832, F835, F840, F842, F844, F846, F848, F850, F852, F854, F856: each pin a one-frame pop

techniques.name: Thrown full-frame sheet
techniques.description: Rotating, growing past the frame, then settling. Used as a one-off break.

techniques.name: Word building up from a rising scan line
techniques.description: A thin coloured scan line rises from low in the word (F1404) at an even rate, drawing on twos, leaving the finished letters behind with an offset colour misregistration; complete in about 32 frames.

ease.name: steps(16)
evidence: visuals/a1/t-scan.jpg F1407-F1435: diff alternates about 1.0 and 0.3, a new drawing every second frame at an even rate (linear on twos)

typography.entry: built upward behind a rising scan line, on twos, with colour misregistration
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 47.52-48.02 box x 0.064 w 0.323 h 0.297

techniques.name: Pull-back with a tilt, and a title that inks in
techniques.description: An eased pull-back with a tilt of about 5 degrees that straightens slowly: starts from rest at F1517 (50.57 s), peaks at 52.6 s and settles by F1640 (54.67 s), about 4.1 s, symmetric. The title sits faint (about 15% contrast) across the pull-back, then snaps to full black at F1678 (55.93 s) under a 12-frame whole-frame flicker.
techniques.routeReason: Same camera as the rest, if the single-sheet approach is built first. It is hard to retrofit.

typography.entry: faint to full black in one frame (F1678), then a 12-frame whole-frame flicker settling by F1690
evidence: speech-text.json screenText 58.02-60.02 box x 0.301 w 0.402 h 0.127

techniques.name: Objects moving on twos and threes under a smooth camera
techniques.description: The machine's entrance changes only on F1117, F1119, F1122, F1125 and F1127, with near-zero differences between (diffMean under 0.7), and then the whole frame settles smoothly. Only checked on this object; other entrances in the film might differ, as the opening's motion changes every frame.
